questions.question: Which club won the 2025 UEFA Champions League?

• The final was held at the **Allianz Arena** in **Munich**, **Germany**, on **May 31, 2025**, which saw a capacity crowd witness the crowning of a new European champion.
 
• **PSG** defeated **Manchester City** in the final with a scoreline of **2-1**, with decisive goals coming from their star-studded lineup.
 
• This victory was the culmination of a decade-long project by the club's ownership, **Qatar Sports Investments**, who acquired the club in **2011** with the primary goal of winning this prestigious trophy.
 
• By winning the title, **Paris Saint-Germain** became only the second **French** club in history to win the competition, joining **Olympique de Marseille** who won it in **1993**.

• The **2024-25** season was the first to implement the new **"Swiss Model"** or **League Phase**, expanding the competition from **32** to **36** teams.

• The **Allianz Arena**, the home of **Bayern Munich**, hosted the final for the first time since the **2012** season.
 
• With a capacity of approximately **75,000**, it remains one of the most modern and iconic football stadiums in **Europe**.

• **Qualification:** As winners of the **2025** final, **PSG** earned an automatic spot in the **2025-26 UEFA Champions League** league phase and a place in the **2025 UEFA Super Cup**.

questions.question: The Republic Day celebrated on 26 January 2025, was India's ________ Republic Day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**76th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India celebrated its **76th Republic Day** on **26 January 2025**. This occasion marks the completion of **75 years** since the **Constitution of India** came into effect in **1950**.
 
• The **76th Republic Day** festivities continue the tradition of showcasing India’s **military prowess**, **cultural heritage**, and **technological advancements** at **Kartavya Path** in **New Delhi**.
 
• The celebration in **2025** is particularly significant as it follows the landmark **‘Platinum Jubilee’** year (75th anniversary) of the Indian Republic, emphasizing the theme of **‘Viksit Bharat’** (Developed India).
 
• The **President of India** unfurls the **National Flag** (Tiranga) at Kartavya Path, followed by the National Anthem and a **21-gun salute** using indigenous field guns.
 
• The parade typically features various **tableaux** from different states and union territories, highlighting the **social and economic progress** of the nation. ***Hence, the correct answer is 76th.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Significance of 26 January:**
 
 
• The date was chosen to honor the **Purna Swaraj** (Complete Independence) declaration by the **Indian National Congress** in **1930** at the **Lahore Session**.
 
• While India gained independence on **15 August 1947**, it remained a **constitutional monarchy** under the **Government of India Act 1935** until the Constitution was officially adopted in **1950**.
 
 
 
• **The Constitution of India:**
 
 
• The **Constituent Assembly** adopted the Constitution on **26 November 1949** (celebrated as **Constitution Day**), but it was legally enforced on **26 January 1950**.
 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, the Chairman of the **Drafting Committee**, is regarded as the **Chief Architect** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The drafting process took **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete, making it the **longest written constitution** of any sovereign country in the world.
 
 
 
• **Key Traditions:**
 
 
• **Chief Guest:** Every year, India invites a **Head of State** from another country as the **Chief Guest** for the Republic Day parade to strengthen **diplomatic ties**.
 
• **Beating Retreat:** The celebrations officially conclude on the evening of **29 January** with the **Beating Retreat Ceremony** at **Vijay Chowk**, featuring performances by the bands of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Awards and Honors:**
 
 
• On the eve of Republic Day, the **President of India** announces the **Padma Awards**, which are the highest civilian honors in the country, categorized into **Padma Vibhushan**, **Padma Bhushan**, and **Padma Shri**.
 
• **Gallantry Awards** such as the **Param Vir Chakra**, **Ashoka Chakra**, and **Vir Chakra** are also conferred upon brave soldiers and civilians during the ceremony.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Framework:**
 
 
• **Article 394** of the Constitution states that the remaining provisions (other than those that came into force on 26 Nov 1949) shall come into force on **26 January 1950**, referred to as the **Commencement of the Constitution**.
 
• The Republic Day symbolizes the transition of India from a **British Dominion** to a **Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: On 12 April 2025, which of the following banks celebrated 131st foundation day with the launch of 34 new banking products and services?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab National Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Punjab National Bank (PNB)** celebrated its **131st Foundation Day** on **12 April 2025**, marking over thirteen decades of service to the nation since its inception in the late **19th century**.
 
• To commemorate this significant milestone, the bank launched **34 new banking products and services** designed to cater to modern retail, agriculture, and **MSME** customers, with a heavy focus on **digital transformation** and **financial inclusion**.
 
• Founded in **1894** and starting its operations on **12 April 1895**, PNB was the first bank to be purely managed by **Indians** with Indian capital, reflecting the spirit of the **Swadeshi Movement**.
 
• The visionary leader **Lala Lajpat Rai** was instrumental in the establishment of the bank, and he was its first account holder, emphasizing the need for an indigenous financial institution during the **British Raj**.
 
• Currently, **Punjab National Bank** is the **second-largest public sector bank** in **India** in terms of total business volume, maintaining a massive network of branches and **ATMs** across the country and a presence in several **international locations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Mergers:** PNB has grown significantly through strategic consolidations, most notably the **mega-merger** effective from **1 April 2020**, which saw the **United Bank of India** and **Oriental Bank of Commerce (OBC)** being integrated into PNB.
 
• **Canara Bank:** Established in **1906** by **Ammembal Subba Rao Pai** in **Mangalore**, it is another major public sector bank. It merged with **Syndicate Bank** in **2020** and is headquartered in **Bengaluru**.
 
• **Bank of India:** Founded on **7 September 1906** by a group of prominent businessmen from **Mumbai**, it remained under private ownership until it was nationalized in **July 1969** along with 13 other banks.
 
• **Indian Bank:** Headquartered in **Chennai**, this bank was established in **1907** as part of the **Swadeshi Movement**. It merged with **Allahabad Bank** in **2020**, making it one of the largest public sector banks in the country.
 
• **Digital Initiatives:** Modern banking relies heavily on technology; PNB has introduced various platforms like **PNB One**, an integrated mobile banking application, and continues to invest in **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Machine Learning** to improve customer service and security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Establishment Date:** While the bank was registered on **19 May 1894**, it officially opened for business on **12 April 1895** in **Lahore** (undivided India).
 
• **The Swadeshi Ethos:** Unlike other banks of that era which were mostly controlled by **European** interests, PNB was a symbol of **Indian self-reliance** and economic nationalism.
 
• **Headquarters:** After the partition in **1947**, the bank shifted its registered office to **New Delhi**, where it continues to operate its central management today.
</ul

questions.question: Which female athlete received the Sportstar of the Year (Female) award in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manu Bhaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Indian ace shooter **Manu Bhaker** was honored with the **Sportstar of the Year (Female)** award at the **Sportstar Aces Awards 2025** for her path-breaking performances.
 
• This recognition primarily stems from her historic feat at the **Paris 2024 Olympic Games**, where she became the first athlete from independent **India** to win **two medals** in a single edition of the **Olympics**.
 
• She secured her first **bronze medal** in the **women’s 10m air pistol** event, followed by another **bronze medal** in the **10m air pistol mixed team** event alongside partner **Sarabjot Singh**.
 
• The award celebrates her resilience after a disappointing outing at the **Tokyo 2020 Olympics**, marking a significant comeback in the international sporting arena.
 
• Her achievements have been instrumental in elevating the status of **shooting** in India, inspiring a new generation of athletes to take up the sport at a professional level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Manu Bhaker:**
 
 
• Born in **February 2002**, in the **Jhajjar** district of **Haryana**, she initially excelled in multiple sports including **Huyen langlon** (a Manipuri martial art), boxing, and skating.
 
• She rose to global prominence at the age of **16** by becoming the youngest Indian to win a **gold medal** at the **ISSF World Cup** in **2018** held in **Guadalajara, Mexico**.
 
• In addition to her **Olympic** medals, she won **gold** at the **2018 Gold Coast Commonwealth Games** and multiple medals at the **Asian Games** and **World Championships**.
 
• She was conferred with the **Arjuna Award** in **2020** for her outstanding contributions to Indian sports.
 
 
 
• **Sportstar Aces Awards:**
 
 
• These awards are an initiative by **The Hindu Group** through its sports magazine, **Sportstar**, to honor the "Spirit of Excellence" in **Indian sports**.
 
• The awards recognize athletes across various categories including **Sportstar of the Year**, **Coach of the Year**, and **Lifetime Achievement** awards.
 
• The selection process usually involves a combination of jury evaluation and popular fan voting to determine the winners based on the performance in the preceding **calendar year**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Olympic Significance:** Manu Bhaker's success at **Paris 2024** ended a **12-year drought** for Indian shooting at the **Olympics**, with the last medals coming in **2012 London** (Vijay Kumar and Gagan Narang).
 
• **Versatility:** While she is famous for the **10m air pistol**, she also competes in the **25m pistol** category, reaching the final of that event as well during the **2024 Olympics**.
 
• **National Impact:** Following her 2024 success, the **National Rifle Association of India (NRAI)** saw a significant surge in registrations, highlighting the "Manu Bhaker effect" on grassroots sports participation in **India**.
 
• **Academic Pursuit:** Despite her rigorous training schedule, she pursued her education at the prestigious **Lady Shri Ram College (LSR)** in **New Delhi**, balancing academics with her professional shooting career.

questions.question: At which place in India was the setting up of the International Potato Center-South Asia Regional Centre (CSARC) approved by the Union Cabinet of India in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Cabinet**, chaired by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, gave its approval for the setting up of the **International Potato Center (CIP)-South Asia Regional Centre (CSARC)** in **Agra**, **Uttar Pradesh**, in **June 2025**.
 
• The establishment of this center follows an agreement between the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE)**, under the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, and the **International Potato Center (CIP)**.
 
• The **CSARC** is intended to be a world-class facility that will serve as a hub for research on **potato** and **sweet potato**, focusing on the specific needs of farmers in **South Asian** countries including **India**, **Bangladesh**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The primary objective of the center is to improve **food and nutrition security** by developing **climate-resilient** and **disease-resistant** varieties of tubers to increase the **yield** and **income** of small-scale farmers.
 
• The **Government of Uttar Pradesh** has played a pivotal role by providing **land** (approximately **10 hectares**) for the setting up of this prestigious international research institute.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Potato Center (CIP):** 
 
 
• Headquartered in **Lima**, **Peru**, it was founded in **1971**.
 
• It is a member of the **CGIAR** (Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research), a global partnership that unites organizations engaged in research for a food-secure future.
 
• CIP maintains the world’s largest **gene bank** for potatoes and sweet potatoes to preserve **biodiversity**.
 
 
 
• **Potato Production in India:** 
 
 
• **India** is the **second-largest producer** of potatoes in the world after **China**.
 
• The state of **Uttar Pradesh** is the **leading producer** of potatoes in India, contributing nearly **30%** of the total national production.
 
• **Agra** and its surrounding districts like **Hathras** and **Aligarh** form the most intensive potato-growing belt in the country, often referred to as the **Potato Bowl of India**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Tubers:** 
 
 
• Potatoes and sweet potatoes are identified as **essential crops** for addressing **malnutrition** and ensuring **calorie intake** for the growing population in developing nations.
 
• The **CSARC** will leverage **digital tools** and **precision agriculture** to modernize the cultivation of these crops.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The establishment of **CSARC** in **Agra** aligns with the **Viksit Bharat 2047** goal of making India a global leader in **agricultural innovation**.
 
• Previously, India established the **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)** South Asia Regional Centre in **Varanasi** in **2018**, which served as a successful model for this potato research center.
 
• The center will facilitate **cross-border collaboration** and **knowledge exchange** between scientists from various **South Asian** nations and international experts.
 
• The **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)**, through the **Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI)** in **Shimla**, will work in close coordination with the new **Agra** center to avoid duplication and maximize research efficiency.

questions.question: As per data released by Ministry of Earth Sciences in March 2025, what percentage of area in India is vulnerable to earthquakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**59%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the data released by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES)** in **March 2025**, approximately **59%** of **India's landmass** is vulnerable to **earthquakes** of moderate to very high intensity.
 
• The assessment is based on the **seismic zoning map** of India, which categorizes the country into different regions based on the historical frequency and intensity of seismic activity.
 
• The **National Center for Seismology (NCS)**, which functions under the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, is the nodal agency for monitoring earthquake activity in **India** and maintains a nationwide network of stations.
 
• The high vulnerability is primarily attributed to the **tectonic plate movements**, specifically the **Indian Plate** moving northward and colliding with the **Eurasian Plate**, leading to significant stress accumulation along the **Himalayan belt**.
 
• This **59%** area includes regions classified under **Zone III, Zone IV, and Zone V**, where **Zone V** represents the highest seismic risk.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seismic Zoning in India:**

 
 
• The **Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)** is the official body that publishes the **Seismic Zoning Map of India** [IS 1893 (Part I): 2016].
 
• **Zone V:** Covers the regions with the highest risk of earthquakes. It includes the entire **North-Eastern India**, parts of **Jammu and Kashmir**, **Himachal Pradesh**, **Uttarakhand**, the **Rann of Kutch** in **Gujarat**, and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
• **Zone IV:** This is the high-damage risk zone. It includes the **Indo-Gangetic basin**, **Delhi**, **Sikkim**, and parts of **Bihar** and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• **Zone III:** This is the moderate-damage risk zone. Many major cities like **Mumbai**, **Kolkata**, and **Chennai** fall under or near this zone.
 
• **Zone II:** This is the low-damage risk zone, covering the remaining parts of the country that are relatively stable.
 
 
 
• **Geological Factors:**
 
 
• The **Indian subcontinent** has a history of devastating earthquakes such as the **2001 Bhuj earthquake**, the **1993 Latur earthquake**, and the **1950 Assam-Tibet earthquake**.
 
• The **Himalayan region** is considered one of the most seismically active regions in the world due to the ongoing **continental collision**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismic Microzonation:** The **Government of India** has initiated **Seismic Microzonation** studies for major cities to identify specific local hazards, which helps in better **urban planning** and **disaster mitigation**.
 
• **Building Codes:** To minimize loss of life, the government emphasizes adherence to **Earthquake Resistant Design** standards for **construction**, especially in high-risk zones.
 
• **Disaster Management:** The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** provides guidelines and protocols for **earthquake preparedness**, response, and **structural safety audits**.
 
• **Monitoring:** As of **2025**, the **NCS** has expanded its network to include over **160 seismic stations** across **India** to provide real-time data and early alerts for major tremors.

questions.question: NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) which was scheduled to be launched from India in July 2025 jointly by National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is a ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**$1.5 billion mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NISAR**, which stands for **NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar**, is a joint earth-observation mission between the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)** of the United States and the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** of India.
 
• The project is estimated to be a **$1.5 billion mission**, making it one of the world's most expensive and advanced earth-imaging satellite missions to date.
 
• The mission was originally conceptualized through a partnership agreement signed in **September 2014**. It is currently scheduled for launch in **July 2025** from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota**, India.
 
• The primary objective of **NISAR** is to use advanced radar imaging to map the entire **Earth** every **12 days**, providing unprecedented data on changes in **ecosystems**, **ice mass**, **vegetation biomass**, and **sea level rise**.
 
• It is designed to observe and measure some of the planet's most complex natural processes, including **natural hazards** such as **earthquakes**, **tsunamis**, **volcanoes**, and **landslides**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Technical Specifications:**
 
 
• **NISAR** is the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies: the **L-band SAR** (provided by **NASA**) and the **S-band SAR** (provided by **ISRO**).
 
• The **L-band** radar can penetrate deep into dense vegetation and is managed by **NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)**, while the **S-band** radar is ideal for monitoring heavy weather and coastal regions.
 
• The satellite features a large **deployable mesh antenna**, approximately **12 meters** in diameter, which will be used to transmit and receive the radar signals.
 
 
 
• **Roles of the Agencies:**
 
 
• **NASA** is responsible for providing the **L-band SAR**, the **high-rate communication subsystem** for science data, **GPS receivers**, and a **solid-state recorder**.
 
• **ISRO** is providing the **S-band SAR**, the **spacecraft bus** (the main body of the satellite), the **launch vehicle** (**GSLV Mark II**), and related launch services.
 
 
 
• **Mission Duration and Impact:**
 
 
• The mission has a planned lifetime of at least **3 years**.
 
• The data collected will be **open-access**, meaning it will be available to the global scientific community to improve **climate change** models and **disaster management** strategies.
 
• It will provide critical information regarding the **rate of melting** of **glaciers** and **ice sheets** in the **Arctic** and **Antarctic** regions, which is essential for predicting **global sea level rise**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **NISAR** mission represents a significant milestone in **India-US space cooperation**, showcasing the ability of both nations to pool financial and technical resources for **global environmental monitoring**.
 
• The **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** technology allows the satellite to "see" through **clouds** and **darkness**, enabling **24/7 observation** of the Earth's surface regardless of weather conditions.
 
• By tracking subtle changes in the Earth's crust (as small as **centimeters**), **NISAR** will help scientists provide better warnings for **volcanic eruptions** and identify areas most at risk during **tectonic shifts**.
</ul

questions.question: In August 2025, which body directed the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) of the Government of India to frame terms for an ozone study committee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Green Tribunal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Green Tribunal (NGT)**, in **August 2025**, directed the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)** to constitute an expert committee and frame its **Terms of Reference (ToR)** for a detailed study on **ground-level ozone**.
 
• The directive comes in response to rising concerns over **ozone (O3)** acting as a dangerous **secondary pollutant**, which is often overshadowed by particulate matter like **PM2.5** and **PM10** in national air quality discussions.
 
• The **NGT** emphasized that there is a lack of adequate monitoring and specific mitigation strategies for **ground-level ozone**, which is primarily formed through chemical reactions in the atmosphere.
 
• The proposed committee is expected to involve representatives and scientists from the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT)**, and other environmental research bodies to analyze the **seasonal variations** and **precursor emissions** of ozone.
 
• The **NGT**'s intervention highlights the necessity for the **Government of India** to update the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** to include more robust protocols for managing gaseous pollutants alongside solid particulates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):**
 
 
• The **NGT** was established on **18th October 2010** under the **National Green Tribunal Act 2010** for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to **environmental protection** and conservation of forests.
 
• It is a specialized body equipped with the necessary expertise to handle **environmental disputes** involving multi-disciplinary issues, and it is not bound by the procedure laid down under the **Code of Civil Procedure, 1908**, but guided by principles of **natural justice**.
 
• The principal bench of the **NGT** is located in **New Delhi**, with regional benches in **Bhopal**, **Pune**, **Kolkata**, and **Chennai**.
 
 
 
• **Ground-Level Ozone (O3):**
 
 
• Unlike the **stratospheric ozone layer** that protects Earth from UV radiation, ground-level ozone is a **harmful air pollutant** and a key constituent of **smog**.
 
• It is not emitted directly but created by chemical reactions between **Oxides of Nitrogen (NOx)** and **Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)** in the presence of **sunlight** and high temperatures.
 
• Significant sources of **NOx** and **VOCs** include **industrial facilities**, electric utilities, **motor vehicle exhaust**, and chemical solvents.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC):**
 
 
• This is the **nodal agency** in the administrative structure of the Central Government for the planning, promotion, and coordination of environmental and **forestry programmes** in India.
 
• It oversees the implementation of the **Environment Protection Act (1986)** and manages the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**, which aims for a **20-40% reduction** in particulate matter concentration by **2026**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Health Impacts:** High concentrations of **ground-level ozone** can cause immediate **respiratory health problems**, including **asthma**, reduced lung function, and increased susceptibility to respiratory infections.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Ozone also affects sensitive **vegetation and ecosystems**, leading to reduced **agricultural crop yields** and interfering with the ability of plants to produce and store food.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981** provides the legal basis for the **CPCB** and **SPCBs** to set standards and monitor air quality, including gaseous pollutants like **O3**, **SO2**, and **NO2**.
</ul

questions.question: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in June 2025 announced its plan to launch the first-ever nationwide household income survey in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2026**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** announced in **June 2025** that it would conduct India's first official nationwide **household income survey**.
 
• The survey is scheduled to be launched in the year **2026**, marking a significant shift in how the country collects economic data.
 
• Historically, **India** has relied on **Household Consumption Expenditure Surveys (HCES)** to estimate poverty and economic well-being, rather than direct income data.
 
• This new initiative aims to provide a more accurate picture of the **standard of living**, **income distribution**, and the **economic gap** between various sections of society.
 
• The **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which functions under **MoSPI**, will be the nodal agency responsible for designing the methodology and executing the fieldwork for this survey. ***Hence, the correct answer is 2026.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):**
 
 
• **MoSPI** came into existence as an independent Ministry on **15th October 1999** after the merger of the Department of Statistics and the Department of Programme Implementation.
 
• It has two wings: one relating to **Statistics** (headed by the **National Statistical Office**) and the other is **Programme Implementation**.
 
• The **Statistics Wing** is responsible for the timely release of critical data such as the **Consumer Price Index (CPI)**, **Index of Industrial Production (IIP)**, and **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** estimates.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Income Surveys:**
 
 
• Direct income surveys help in calculating the **Gini Coefficient**, which is a standard mathematical measure of **income inequality** within a nation.
 
• Currently, organizations like **ICE 360** (People Research on India's Consumer Economy) conduct private income surveys, but an official government survey will provide **authentic data** for **policy formulation**.
 
• This data is vital for tailoring **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** schemes and identifying the **beneficiaries** of various social welfare programs more effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Consumption Data:**
 
 
• While **consumption expenditure** tracks what households spend, an **income survey** tracks what they earn from all sources including **wages**, **agriculture**, **business**, and **investments**.
 
• The transition to income-based tracking aligns **India** with international statistical standards followed by many **developed nations** and **OECD countries**.
 
 
 
• **Other Major Surveys by MoSPI:**
 
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):** Launched in **April 2017**, it provides estimates of **unemployment rates** and labour force participation at frequent intervals.
 
• **Annual Survey of Industries (ASI):** The principal source of industrial statistics in **India**, providing information on the growth and structure of the **manufacturing sector**.
 
• **Economic Census:** Conducted periodically to provide a complete count of all **entrepreneurial units** (establishments) located within the geographical boundaries of the country.
 
 
 
• **Timeline Context:**
 
 
• The decision in **June 2025** to start the survey in **2026** follows recommendations from various **Expert Committees** that suggested India needs a dedicated income database to complement its **decadal Census** and **NFHS (National Family Health Survey)** data.
 
 
</ul
